records.literal_gloss: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, on shigionoth.

en.L: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, on shigionoth.
en.B: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, on shigionoth.
en.R: A prayer of the prophet Habakkuk, to be sung as a song.

pt.L: Oração de Habacuque, o profeta, sobre Sigionote.
pt.B: Oração do profeta Habacuque, sobre Sigionote.
pt.R: Oração do profeta Habacuque, para ser cantada como canção.

decisions.choice: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet: a psalm, with a title like those of the Psalms
decisions.reason: Chapter 3 is a psalm. It has a title naming its author and the kind of song (as Psalm 7:1), "Selah" three times (verses 3, 9, 13), and a closing note for the music director (verse 19), like the titles of Psalm 4:1 and others. Psalms 17, 86, 90 and 102 are also called "prayers". It was evidently used in worship. The prophet answers God's word in chapter 2 with praise and trust.

decisions.choice: on shigionoth: a musical term whose sense is unknown
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of "shiggaion", the term in the title of Psalm 7, and is used only here. It names a kind of song or a tune; some link it with a verb for wandering or reeling, others with a word for lament. "On" may mean "set to" or "in the style of".

decisions.choice: shigionoth (L, B); to be sung as a song (R)
decisions.reason: As "shiggaion" in Psalm 7:1, Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew word, and Readable says only that it is a song, since the exact sense is unknown (m2). The title is its own verse and stays as one line.

decisions.choice: Oração ... sobre Sigionote (L, B); para ser cantada como canção (R)
decisions.reason: The heading is set like a psalm title (m1). The musical term is the plural of "Sigaiom", which Psalm 7:1 keeps in a Portuguese spelling (m2), so Literal and Balanced keep it as "Sigionote", capitalised as the name of a kind of song as in Psalm 7:1; Readable says only that it is a song, as the English does.

source.text: יְהוָ֗ה שָׁמַ֣עְתִּי שִׁמְעֲךָ֮ יָרֵאתִי֒ יְהוָ֗ה פָּֽעָלְךָ֙ בְּקֶ֤רֶב שָׁנִים֙ חַיֵּ֔יהוּ בְּקֶ֥רֶב שָׁנִ֖ים תּוֹדִ֑יעַ בְּרֹ֖גֶז רַחֵ֥ם תִּזְכּֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh, I have heard your report; I fear. Yahweh, your work, in [the] midst of years revive it; in [the] midst of years make [it] known; in wrath, to have compassion remember.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I have heard the report of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; I am afraid. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} work, in the midst of [the] years revive it; \q in the midst of [the] years make [it] known; \q in rage remember to have compassion.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I have heard of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fame, and I stand in awe. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, renew {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} work in our own time; \q in our own time make it known; \q in wrath, remember mercy.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I have heard about what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done, and I am filled with awe. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do those great things again in our time. \q Let people see them in our day. \q Even when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are angry, remember to show mercy.

pt.L: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, ouvi a notícia a {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} respeito; tenho medo. \q {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} obra, no meio dos anos, faze-a reviver; \q no meio dos anos, dá-[a] a conhecer; \q na ira, lembra-te de ter compaixão.
pt.B: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, ouvi falar da {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} fama, e fico cheio de temor. \q {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, renova a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} obra no nosso tempo; \q no nosso tempo, torna-a conhecida; \q na ira, lembra-te da compaixão.
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, ouvi falar do que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fizeste, e estou cheio de temor. \q {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, faze de novo aquelas grandes coisas no nosso tempo. \q Deixa que as pessoas as vejam nos nossos dias. \q Mesmo quando {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} estiveres irado, lembra-te de mostrar compaixão.

decisions.choice: I have heard the report of you; I am afraid: awe at what God has done
decisions.reason: "Report" is what Habakkuk has heard of the LORD: his deeds in the past, such as the exodus (verses 3-15), and his word in chapter 2. "I am afraid" is the trembling awe of one who knows God's power (verse 16).

decisions.choice: in the midst of the years: in our own time
decisions.reason: Habakkuk asks God to do again, in his own day, the mighty work he did in the past, rather than leaving it in history. "Revive it" means bring it to life again.

decisions.choice: in wrath remember mercy
decisions.reason: The word for "mercy" is the tender compassion of a parent (Psalm 103:13). Habakkuk accepts that judgment is coming (1:12; 3:16) and asks that God's anger be tempered with compassion for his people.

decisions.choice: fame (B); what you have done (R); renew, in our own time (B); do those great things again (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "report" was (m1) and what "in the midst of the years" means (m2).

decisions.choice: tu, with deity_pronoun spans, through the prayer; compaixão
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter: the prayer speaks to God with "tu", as the Psalms do in Portuguese (see 1:2), and the vocative "SENHOR" stands without "ó", as in the English. The word for mercy is the tender compassion of a parent (m3), so every level says "compaixão"; the wording of verses 2 and 17-19 was drafted from the Hebrew away from the familiar Portuguese versions.

source.text: אֱל֨וֹהַ֙מִתֵּימָ֣ן יָב֔וֹא וְקָד֥וֹשׁ מֵֽהַר־פָּארָ֖ן סֶ֑לָה כִּסָּ֤ה שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ הוֹד֔וֹ וּתְהִלָּת֖וֹ מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: God from Teman comes, and [the] Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His splendor covered [the] heavens, and his praise filled the earth.

en.L: God came from Teman, \q and the Holy One from Mount Paran. \q His splendor covered the heavens, \q and the earth was full of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise. Selah
en.B: God came from Teman, \q the Holy One from Mount Paran. \q His splendor covered the heavens, \q and the earth was filled with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise. Selah
en.R: God came from the land of Teman. \q The Holy God came from Mount Paran. \q His glory covered the sky, \q and the earth was full of praise for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Selah

pt.L: Deus veio de Temã, \q e o Santo, do monte Parã. \q O {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} esplendor cobriu os céus, \q e a terra se encheu do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} louvor. Selá
pt.B: Deus veio de Temã, \q o Santo veio do monte Parã. \q O {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} esplendor cobriu os céus, \q e a terra ficou cheia do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} louvor. Selá
pt.R: Deus veio da terra de Temã. \q O Deus Santo veio do monte Parã. \q A {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} glória cobriu o céu, \q e a terra se encheu de louvor a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. Selá

decisions.choice: God came from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran: as when he came from Sinai
decisions.reason: Teman is a region of Edom, south of Judah (Jeremiah 49:7; Obadiah 9), and Paran the wilderness between Sinai and Canaan (Numbers 10:12). Older poems picture the LORD marching from the south, from Sinai, Seir and Paran, to help his people (Deuteronomy 33:2; Judges 5:4; Psalm 68:8-9). Habakkuk recalls that coming in verses 3-15. The word for "God" here is a rare, poetic form.

decisions.choice: came: the poem tells what God did, in the language of vision
alternatives: God comes: a vision of a future coming
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verbs of verses 3-15 shift between forms that can be past, present or future. The poem recalls God's coming at the exodus and Sinai, and pictures it as if seen anew; Habakkuk hopes to see the same again (verse 2). The translation tells it as past.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in this chapter (verses 3, 9 and 13). It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude. It is not part of what is said.

decisions.choice: Selah moved to the end
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts Selah in the middle of the verse, after the first line. Every level puts it at the end so that the verse reads as a whole, as in Psalm 57:4.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (m3), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

decisions.choice: Temã, Parã; Selá (at the end of the verse)
decisions.reason: Teman takes the form of Jeremiah 49:7 and Obadiah 9, and Paran its usual Portuguese form (m1). "Selá" is kept at every level in the spelling the Psalms use, set at the end of the verse as the English sets it (m3), here and in verses 9 and 13.

source.text: וְנֹ֨גַהּ֙ כָּא֣וֹר תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה קַרְנַ֥יִם מִיָּד֖וֹ ל֑וֹ וְשָׁ֖ם חֶבְי֥וֹן עֻזֹּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And brightness like the light was; two horns from his hand [belong] to him; and there [was the] hiding of his power.

en.L: And [his] brightness was like the light; \q rays [came] from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, \q and there {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power was hidden.
en.B: His brightness was like the sunlight; \q rays flashed from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, \q and there {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power lay hidden.
en.R: He was as bright as the sun. \q Rays of light came from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, \q where {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power was hidden.

pt.L: E [o seu] brilho era como a luz; \q raios [saíam] da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão, \q e ali estava escondido o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} poder.
pt.B: O {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} brilho era como a luz do sol; \q raios saíam da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão, \q e ali o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} poder se escondia.
pt.R: Ele brilhava como o sol. \q Raios de luz saíam da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão, \q onde o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} poder estava escondido.

decisions.choice: rays from his hand
decisions.reason: The word usually means "horns". The related verb is used of Moses' face shining with rays of light (Exodus 34:29), so here it is rays of light, like lightning, flashing from God's hand. "Horns" are also a picture of strength (Psalm 18:3).

decisions.choice: there his power was hidden
decisions.reason: The light that shone from God was only the covering of a power greater still, which no one can see (Exodus 33:20-23; Psalm 18:12).

decisions.choice: [his] brightness (L); sunlight (B); as bright as the sun (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "brightness" without "his"; Literal brackets it. The light is the light of day, the sun, as Balanced and Readable say.

source.text: לְפָנָ֖יו יֵ֣לֶךְ דָּ֑בֶר וְיֵצֵ֥א רֶ֖שֶׁף לְרַגְלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Before him went pestilence, and plague went out at his feet.

en.L: Before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} went pestilence, \q and plague went out at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.
en.B: Disease went ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and plague followed at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heels.
en.R: Disease went ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and plague followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

pt.L: Diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} ia a peste, \q e a praga saía aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés.
pt.B: A doença ia à frente {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, \q e a praga seguia nos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} calcanhares.
pt.R: A doença ia na frente {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, \q e a praga vinha atrás {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.

decisions.choice: pestilence and plague: attendants of the divine warrior
decisions.reason: Pestilence and plague are pictured as servants who go before and behind a king (Psalm 78:48-50; Deuteronomy 32:24). The second word is also the name of a god of plague worshiped by Israel's neighbors; here plague is no god but the LORD's servant. The plagues of Egypt may be in mind (Exodus 9:3, 15).

decisions.choice: Disease (B, R); at his heels (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "disease" for the older "pestilence". "At his feet" means close behind him, at his heels.

source.text: עָמַ֣ד׀וַיְמֹ֣דֶד אֶ֗רֶץ רָאָה֙ וַיַּתֵּ֣ר גּוֹיִ֔ם וַיִּתְפֹּֽצְצוּ֙ הַרְרֵי־עַ֔ד שַׁח֖וּ גִּבְע֣וֹת עוֹלָ֑ם הֲלִיכ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: He stood and shook [the] earth; he looked and made nations leap; and [the] mountains of antiquity were shattered; [the] hills of antiquity bowed down; [the] goings of antiquity [belong] to him.

en.L: He stood and shook [the] earth; he saw and made [the] nations leap; \q and the age-old mountains were shattered; \q the everlasting hills sank low; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways [are] everlasting.
en.B: He stood, and the earth shook; he looked, and the nations trembled. \q The ancient mountains broke apart; \q the age-old hills sank down. \q His ways are eternal.
en.R: He stood up and made the earth shake. He looked, and the nations trembled. \q The mountains that had stood for ages broke apart. \q The ancient hills sank down. \q His ways are eternal.

pt.L: Ele parou e sacudiu [a] terra; olhou e fez saltar as nações; \q e os montes antigos se despedaçaram; \q as colinas eternas se abateram; \q os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} caminhos [são] eternos.
pt.B: Ele parou, e a terra tremeu; olhou, e as nações estremeceram. \q Os montes antigos se partiram; \q as colinas de outrora afundaram. \q Os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} caminhos são eternos.
pt.R: Ele se levantou e fez a terra tremer. Olhou, e as nações tremeram. \q Os montes que existiam havia séculos se partiram. \q As colinas antigas afundaram. \q Os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} caminhos são eternos.

decisions.choice: shook the earth
alternatives: he stood and measured the earth
decisions.reason: The verb may come from a root meaning "measure" (he stood and measured the earth) or from one meaning "shake". The shaking of the earth fits the next lines.

decisions.choice: the age-old mountains ... the everlasting hills: what seems most permanent gives way
decisions.reason: The mountains and hills are called ancient and everlasting because nothing in the world seems more lasting (Genesis 49:26; Deuteronomy 33:15). They break and sink before the eternal God.

decisions.choice: his ways are everlasting
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean that his ways are eternal, or that the ancient paths, the roads he walked when he came from Sinai, are his.

decisions.choice: the earth shook ... the nations trembled (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what happened when he stood and looked; "made the nations leap" means made them start up in fear.

source.text: תַּ֣חַת אָ֔וֶן רָאִ֖יתִי אָהֳלֵ֣י כוּשָׁ֑ן יִרְגְּז֕וּן יְרִיע֖וֹת אֶ֥רֶץ מִדְיָֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Under trouble I saw [the] tents of Cushan; trembled [the] tent curtains of [the] land of Midian.

en.L: Under distress I saw the tents of Cushan; \q the tent curtains of the land of Midian trembled.
en.B: I saw the tents of Cushan in distress; \q the tent curtains of Midian shook.
en.R: I saw the people of Cushan in their tents, full of fear. \q The people of Midian trembled in their tents.

pt.L: Debaixo de aflição vi as tendas de Cuxã; \q as cortinas das tendas da terra de Midiã tremeram.
pt.B: Vi as tendas de Cuxã em aflição; \q as cortinas das tendas de Midiã estremeceram.
pt.R: Vi o povo de Cuxã nas suas tendas, cheio de medo. \q O povo de Midiã tremia nas suas tendas.

decisions.choice: Cushan and Midian: desert peoples on the route from Sinai
decisions.reason: Midian lay east and south of Edom, in the region where Moses had lived (Exodus 2:15; 3:1). Cushan is named only here; it is set beside Midian and was probably a people of the same region (compare Numbers 12:1, where Moses' wife, a Midianite, may be called a Cushite). The tribes along God's route tremble as he passes.

decisions.choice: I saw: the prophet sees the vision
decisions.reason: Habakkuk speaks as one who sees God's coming before his eyes.

decisions.choice: the people of Cushan in their tents; The people of Midian (R)
decisions.reason: The tents and tent curtains stand for the people who live in them; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: Cuxã; Midiã
decisions.reason: Midian is "Midiã", as the Old Testament terms set it; Cushan, named only here (m1), is "Cuxã", the Portuguese spelling of its sounds, kept apart from "Cuxe" (Cush, Psalm 7:1, Nahum 3:9).

source.text: הֲבִנְהָרִים֙ חָרָ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה אִ֤ם בַּנְּהָרִים֙ אַפֶּ֔ךָ אִם־בַּיָּ֖ם עֶבְרָתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֤י תִרְכַּב֙ עַל־סוּסֶ֔יךָ מַרְכְּבֹתֶ֖יךָ יְשׁוּעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Was it against rivers [that] it burned, Yahweh? Or [is] against the rivers your anger, or against the sea your fury, that you ride on your horses, your chariots of salvation?

en.L: Was it against [the] rivers [that anger] burned, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}? \q Or [was] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger against the rivers, \q or {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury against the sea, \q when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rode on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} horses, \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chariots of salvation?
en.B: Was {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger burning against the rivers, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}? \q Was {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath against the streams, \q or {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury against the sea, \q as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rode {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} horses, \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chariots of salvation?
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, were {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} angry with the rivers? \q Were {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} angry with the streams? \q Were {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} furious with the sea \q when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rode on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} horses \q and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chariots to save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people?

pt.L: Foi contra [os] rios que [a ira] se acendeu, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}? \q Ou [foi] a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} ira contra os rios, \q ou o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} furor contra o mar, \q quando {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} cavalgavas os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} cavalos, \q os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} carros de salvação?
pt.B: A {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} ira se acendia contra os rios, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}? \q Era a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} cólera contra as correntes, \q ou o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} furor contra o mar, \q quando {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} montavas os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} cavalos, \q os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} carros de salvação?
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} estavas irado com os rios? \q Estavas irado com as correntes? \q Estavas furioso com o mar \q quando {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} montavas os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} cavalos \q e ias nos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} carros para salvar o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo?

decisions.choice: the rivers and the sea: the Red Sea and the Jordan
decisions.reason: The questions recall how the sea fled and the Jordan turned back before the LORD when he brought Israel out of Egypt and into the land (Exodus 14-15; Joshua 3; Psalm 114:3-5). The poem also uses the old picture of the sea and rivers as powers of chaos that God subdues (Psalm 74:13-14; 93:3-4). The answer to the questions is no: his anger was against his people's enemies (verses 12-13).

decisions.choice: you rode on your horses, your chariots of salvation: God as a warrior
decisions.reason: The LORD is pictured as a warrior in a chariot, riding the clouds and storm to rescue his people (Deuteronomy 33:26; Psalm 18:11; 68:5).

decisions.choice: salvation: rescue and victory
decisions.reason: The word is rescue from enemies, which is also victory over them; it returns in verses 13 and 18.

decisions.choice: the vocative LORD with no "O"; [that anger] (L); your anger (B); angry (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Psalms, the LORD is addressed without "O". The Hebrew says only "Did it burn", which is said of anger; Literal brackets the word.

source.text: עֶרְיָ֤ה תֵעוֹר֙ קַשְׁתֶּ֔ךָ שְׁבֻע֥וֹת מַטּ֖וֹת אֹ֣מֶר סֶ֑לָה נְהָר֖וֹת תְּבַקַּע־אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Bareness, is made bare your bow; oaths, rods, a word. Selah. [With] rivers you split [the] earth.

en.L: Your bow was laid bare; \q [the] arrows [were] sworn [by] a word. \q With rivers {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} split [the] earth. Selah
en.B: Your bow was drawn from its case; \q the arrows were charged by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word. \q You split the earth with rivers. Selah
en.R: You took out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} bow \q and commanded {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows to fly. \q You split open the earth, and rivers flowed out. Selah

pt.L: O {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} arco foi desnudado; \q [as] flechas [foram] juradas [pela] palavra. \q Com rios {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fendeste [a] terra. Selá
pt.B: O {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} arco foi tirado da capa; \q as flechas receberam a ordem da {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} palavra. \q Fendeste a terra com rios. Selá
pt.R: Tiraste o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} arco \q e mandaste as {{deity_pronoun:tuas|Tuas}} flechas voar. \q Abriste a terra, e rios correram dela. Selá

decisions.choice: [the] arrows [were] sworn [by] a word: a very obscure line
alternatives: you filled your quiver with arrows
the oaths to the tribes were a sure word
decisions.reason: The middle line is three nouns: "oaths" (or "sated" or "sevens"), "rods" (which can mean arrows, staffs or tribes) and "word" (or "command"). It is one of the hardest lines in the Bible to understand. It is taken here to mean that God's arrows were sent out under his command, as if sworn to their task. Other readings are "the rods of chastisement were sworn by your word", "you filled your quiver with arrows", and "oaths were sworn to the tribes". The sense of the verse as a whole is clear: God takes up his weapons.

decisions.choice: with rivers you split the earth
decisions.reason: The earth was split as water burst out, perhaps recalling water from the rock in the wilderness (Exodus 17:6; Psalm 78:15-16) or the opening of springs and rivers in the storm (Psalm 74:15).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in this chapter (verses 3, 9 and 13). It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude. It is not part of what is said.

decisions.choice: Selah moved to the end
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts Selah after the second line. Every level puts it at the end of the verse, as in verse 3, and keeps the word as it is (see verse 3).

decisions.choice: drawn from its case (B); took out your bow (R); charged by your word, commanded your arrows (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Laid bare" means taken from its cover, ready for use. Balanced and Readable follow the reading in m1.

source.text: רָא֤וּךָ יָחִ֨ילוּ֙ הָרִ֔ים זֶ֥רֶם מַ֖יִם עָבָ֑ר נָתַ֤ן תְּהוֹם֙ קוֹל֔וֹ ר֖וֹם יָדֵ֥יהוּ נָשָֽׂא׃

records.literal_gloss: They saw you; they writhe, mountains; a downpour of water passed over; gave the deep its voice; [on] high its hands it lifted.

en.L: [The] mountains saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; they writhed; \q a downpour of water passed by; \q the deep gave its voice; \q it lifted its hands on high.
en.B: The mountains saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and writhed; \q a torrent of water swept past; \q the deep roared aloud \q and lifted its hands high.
en.R: When the mountains saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, they shook. \q Floods of water rushed by. \q The deep ocean roared \q and raised its waves high.

pt.L: [Os] montes {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} viram; contorceram-se; \q um aguaceiro passou; \q o abismo deu a sua voz; \q para o alto levantou as suas mãos.
pt.B: Os montes {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} viram e se contorceram; \q uma torrente de água passou; \q o abismo rugiu bem alto \q e levantou as mãos para o alto.
pt.R: Quando os montes {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} viram, tremeram. \q Enchentes de água passaram correndo. \q O oceano profundo rugiu \q e levantou bem alto as suas ondas.

decisions.choice: the mountains saw you and writhed ... the deep gave its voice: Psalm 77:17-19
decisions.reason: Psalm 77:17-19 says: "The waters saw you, God; ... the deeps trembled", with storm and thunder, in a psalm that also recalls the exodus. Habakkuk applies the picture to the mountains and the deep.

decisions.choice: it lifted its hands on high: the deep raised its waves
decisions.reason: The deep is pictured as a living thing that cries out and lifts its hands, perhaps in fear or surrender. The picture is of its waves rising high.

decisions.choice: raised its waves high
decisions.reason: Readable says what the deep's "hands" are (m2).

decisions.choice: te viram ... se contorceram; o abismo
decisions.reason: The picture echoes Psalm 77:17 (m1), and Literal and Balanced keep that verse's Portuguese words: "te viram", "se contorceram", "o abismo" for the deep.

source.text: שֶׁ֥מֶשׁ יָרֵ֖חַ עָ֣מַד זְבֻ֑לָה לְא֤וֹר חִצֶּ֨יךָ֙ יְהַלֵּ֔כוּ לְנֹ֖גַהּ בְּרַ֥ק חֲנִיתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Sun, moon stood still [in their] dwelling; at [the] light of your arrows they went, at [the] brightness of [the] lightning of your spear.

en.L: Sun [and] moon stood still in [their] dwelling \q at the light of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows [as] they flew, \q at the gleam of the lightning of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} spear.
en.B: Sun and moon stood still in the heavens \q at the light of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} flying arrows, \q at the flash of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} gleaming spear.
en.R: The sun and moon stopped in the sky \q when they saw {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows flash by \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} spear shine like lightning.

pt.L: [O] sol [e a] lua pararam na [sua] morada, \q à luz das {{deity_pronoun:tuas|Tuas}} flechas [que] voavam, \q ao brilho do relâmpago da {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} lança.
pt.B: O sol e a lua pararam no céu \q diante da luz das {{deity_pronoun:tuas|Tuas}} flechas que voavam, \q diante do clarão da {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} lança reluzente.
pt.R: O sol e a lua pararam no céu \q quando viram as {{deity_pronoun:tuas|Tuas}} flechas passando como um raio \q e a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} lança brilhando como relâmpago.

decisions.choice: sun and moon stood still: the battle of Gibeon
decisions.reason: When Joshua fought at Gibeon, "the sun stood still, and the moon stopped" until Israel had won (Joshua 10:12-13). Habakkuk recalls it among the LORD's acts for his people. "Dwelling" is their lofty home in the sky.

decisions.choice: your arrows ... your spear: lightning
decisions.reason: God's arrows and spear are the lightning of the storm (Psalm 18:15; 77:18-19). Their light outshines the sun and moon.

decisions.choice: in the sky (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "in the sky" for "in their dwelling" (m1).

records.literal_gloss: In indignation you march through [the] earth; in anger you thresh nations.

en.L: In indignation {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} marched through [the] earth; \q in anger {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} threshed [the] nations.
en.B: In fury {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} strode across the earth; \q in anger {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} trampled the nations.
en.R: You were angry as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} marched across the earth. \q In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} crushed the nations like grain.

pt.L: Com indignação {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} marchaste pela terra; \q com ira {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} trilhaste as nações.
pt.B: Com fúria {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} atravessaste a terra; \q com ira {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pisoteaste as nações.
pt.R: Estavas irado quando {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} marchaste pela terra. \q Na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} ira {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} esmagaste as nações como se esmaga o trigo.

decisions.choice: you threshed the nations
decisions.reason: Threshing was done by animals treading the grain or by a heavy sledge dragged over it. It is a picture of crushing defeat (Micah 4:13; Isaiah 41:15; Amos 1:3).

decisions.choice: trampled (B); crushed ... like grain (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "trampled"; Readable keeps the threshing picture by saying "like grain".

source.text: יָצָ֨אתָ֙ לְיֵ֣שַׁע עַמֶּ֔ךָ לְיֵ֖שַׁע אֶת־מְשִׁיחֶ֑ךָ מָחַ֤צְתָּ רֹּאשׁ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית רָשָׁ֔ע עָר֛וֹת יְס֥וֹד עַד־צַוָּ֖אר סֶֽלָה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: You went out for [the] salvation of your people, for [the] salvation of your anointed; you crushed [the] head from [the] house of [the] wicked, laying bare [the] foundation to [the] neck. Selah.

en.L: You went forth for [the] salvation of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, \q for saving {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} smashed [the] head from [the] house of [the] wicked, \q laying [it] bare from foundation to neck. Selah
en.B: You went out to save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, \q to save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed one. \q You crushed the head of the house of the wicked, \q stripping it bare from the foundation up to the neck. Selah
en.R: You came out to save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, \q to save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chosen king. \q You crushed the leader of the wicked nation \q and destroyed his house completely, from top to bottom. Selah

pt.L: Saíste para [a] salvação do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo, \q para salvar o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} ungido; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} esmagaste [a] cabeça da casa do ímpio, \q desnudando[-a] do alicerce ao pescoço. Selá
pt.B: Saíste para salvar o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo, \q para salvar o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} ungido. \q Esmagaste a cabeça da casa do ímpio, \q deixando-a desnuda do alicerce até o pescoço. Selá
pt.R: Saíste para salvar o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo, \q para salvar o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} rei escolhido. \q Esmagaste o líder da nação perversa \q e destruíste completamente a casa dele, de cima a baixo. Selá

decisions.choice: your anointed: the king
decisions.reason: The anointed one is the king of God's people, anointed with oil when he was made king (1 Samuel 16:13; Psalm 2:2; 18:51). In this line it stands in parallel with "your people", so the king may stand for the people as a whole (Psalm 28:8). The poem does not name a particular king.

decisions.choice: crushed the head of the house of the wicked, laying it bare from foundation to neck: total defeat
decisions.reason: Two pictures are joined: a house demolished down to its foundations, and an enemy struck on the head and stripped. The "head" is the leader of the wicked nation; the line says that he and his house are destroyed completely. The details of the line are uncertain.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in this chapter (verses 3, 9 and 13). It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude. It is not part of what is said.

decisions.choice: anointed (L, B); chosen king (R)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah 45:1, Readable says "chosen" for "anointed", and adds "king" (m1). The anointed one takes no deity_pronoun span. Selah stays at the end of the verse, as the Hebrew has it.

decisions.choice: the leader of the wicked nation ... from top to bottom
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two pictures mean (m2).

source.text: נָקַ֤בְתָּ בְמַטָּיו֙ רֹ֣אשׁ פְּרָזָ֔יו יִסְעֲר֖וּ לַהֲפִיצֵ֑נִי עֲלִ֣יצֻתָ֔ם כְּמוֹ־לֶאֱכֹ֥ל עָנִ֖י בַּמִּסְתָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: You pierced with his shafts [the] head of his warriors; they storm to scatter me; their exultation [was] as to devour [the] afflicted in secret.

en.L: You pierced with his own shafts the head of his warriors \q [when] they stormed out to scatter me, \q their exulting [was] as [if] to devour \q the afflicted in [a] hiding place.
en.B: With his own arrows {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} pierced the head of his warriors \q when they stormed out to scatter me, \q gloating as if about to devour \q the helpless in their hiding place.
en.R: You used the enemy's own weapons to kill the leader of his soldiers \q when they rushed out like a storm to scatter me. \q They were happy, like someone about to attack \q a poor person who is hiding.

pt.L: Traspassaste com as próprias flechas dele a cabeça dos seus guerreiros, \q [quando] avançaram como tempestade para me dispersar; \q o seu exultar [era] como [se fossem] devorar \q o oprimido em [um] esconderijo.
pt.B: Com as próprias flechas dele {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} traspassaste a cabeça dos seus guerreiros, \q quando avançaram como tempestade para me dispersar, \q exultando como quem está prestes a devorar \q o indefeso no seu esconderijo.
pt.R: Usaste as próprias armas do inimigo para matar o chefe dos seus soldados, \q quando eles vieram como uma tempestade para me espalhar. \q Estavam felizes, como alguém que está prestes a atacar \q um pobre que está escondido.

decisions.choice: with his own shafts the head of his warriors: an obscure line
alternatives: with your arrows you pierced the head of his leaders
decisions.reason: The word for "shafts" is the one translated "arrows" in verse 9; it can also mean staffs. The word for "warriors" is rare and uncertain: it may mean warriors, leaders or villagers. The line seems to say that God turned the enemy's own weapons against him, as when enemies destroyed one another (Judges 7:22; 1 Samuel 14:20). The written text and the reading in the margin differ slightly in one word without changing the sense.

decisions.choice: to scatter me: the prophet speaks for his people
decisions.reason: Habakkuk says "me", speaking as one of the people whom the enemy came to scatter.

decisions.choice: as if to devour the afflicted in a hiding place
decisions.reason: The enemy is pictured as a robber or a lion lying in wait to seize the helpless (Psalm 10:8-9; 17:12).

decisions.choice: the enemy's own weapons; the leader of his soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the line seems to mean (m1).

source.text: דָּרַ֥כְתָּ בַיָּ֖ם סוּסֶ֑יךָ חֹ֖מֶר מַ֥יִם רַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: You trod on the sea [with] your horses, [the] heap of waters many.

en.L: You trod on the sea with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} horses, \q the heaping of many waters.
en.B: You trampled the sea with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} horses, \q churning the mighty waters.
en.R: You rode {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} horses across the sea, \q stirring up the great waters.

pt.L: Pisaste o mar com os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} cavalos, \q o amontoado de muitas águas.
pt.B: Pisoteaste o mar com os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} cavalos, \q agitando as águas poderosas.
pt.R: Atravessaste o mar montado nos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} cavalos, \q agitando as grandes águas.

decisions.choice: you trod on the sea: the crossing of the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The poem returns to the sea of verse 8. At the exodus "the waters were heaped up" (Exodus 15:8), and "your way was through the sea, your path through the great waters" (Psalm 77:20). The word for "heaping" may also mean the foaming or surging of the water.

decisions.choice: churning (B); stirring up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the heaped, surging water as churned or stirred up by the horses.

source.text: שָׁמַ֣עְתִּי׀וַתִּרְגַּ֣ז בִּטְנִ֗י לְקוֹל֙ צָלֲל֣וּ שְׂפָתַ֔י יָב֥וֹא רָקָ֛ב בַּעֲצָמַ֖י וְתַחְתַּ֣י אֶרְגָּ֑ז אֲשֶׁ֤ר אָנ֨וּחַ֙ לְי֣וֹם צָרָ֔ה לַעֲל֖וֹת לְעַ֥ם יְגוּדֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: I heard, and my belly trembled; at [the] sound my lips quivered; rottenness entered into my bones, and under me I trembled, [so] that I will wait quietly for [the] day of distress, to come up on [the] people [who] invade us.

en.L: I heard, and my belly trembled; at the sound my lips quivered; \q rottenness entered my bones, and where I stood I trembled; \q yet I will wait quietly for [the] day of distress \q to come up on [the] people [who] invade us.
en.B: I heard, and my body trembled; my lips quivered at the sound. \q Decay entered my bones, and my legs shook beneath me. \q Yet I will wait quietly for the day of trouble \q to come on the people who invade us.
en.R: When I heard this, my whole body shook. My lips trembled with fear. \q My bones felt weak, and my legs shook under me. \q But I will wait calmly for the day of disaster \q that will come on the nation that attacks us.

pt.L: Ouvi, e o meu ventre tremeu; ao som, os meus lábios estremeceram; \q a podridão entrou nos meus ossos, e onde eu estava tremi; \q contudo, esperarei tranquilo o dia da aflição \q que subirá contra o povo que nos invade.
pt.B: Ouvi, e o meu corpo tremeu; os meus lábios estremeceram com o som. \q A podridão entrou nos meus ossos, e as minhas pernas tremeram debaixo de mim. \q Mesmo assim, esperarei tranquilo o dia da aflição \q que virá sobre o povo que nos invade.
pt.R: Quando ouvi isso, o meu corpo inteiro tremeu. Os meus lábios tremeram de medo. \q Os meus ossos ficaram fracos, e as minhas pernas tremeram. \q Mas vou esperar com calma o dia da desgraça \q que virá sobre a nação que nos ataca.

decisions.choice: belly, lips, bones: terror felt through the whole body
decisions.reason: Habakkuk describes overwhelming fear in bodily terms, as Jeremiah 23:9 and Daniel 10:8 do. The "belly" is the inner body; "rottenness in the bones" means that strength has drained away (Proverbs 12:4; 14:30).

decisions.choice: yet I will wait quietly for the day of distress
alternatives: I tremble because I must wait for the day of distress
decisions.reason: The word that joins the lines can mean "yet", "so that" or "because". It is taken here to mean that, though he trembles, he will wait calmly for the day when distress comes on the invader, as the vision promised (2:3). It may also mean that he trembles because he must wait through the day of distress coming on his own people.

decisions.choice: my body (B, R); my legs shook beneath me (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "body" for "belly" and turn "under me I trembled" into the plain sense: his legs gave way.

source.text: כִּֽי־תְאֵנָ֣ה לֹֽא־תִפְרָ֗ח וְאֵ֤ין יְבוּל֙ בַּגְּפָנִ֔ים כִּחֵשׁ֙ מַעֲשֵׂה־זַ֔יִת וּשְׁדֵמ֖וֹת לֹא־עָ֣שָׂה אֹ֑כֶל גָּזַ֤ר מִמִּכְלָה֙ צֹ֔אן וְאֵ֥ין בָּקָ֖ר בָּרְפָתִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For [the] fig tree not does blossom, and there is no produce on the vines; fails [the] yield of [the] olive, and fields not do produce food; is cut off from [the] fold [the] flock, and there are no cattle in the stalls,

en.L: Though [the] fig tree does not blossom and there is no fruit on the vines, \q [though the] yield of [the] olive fails \q and [the] fields do not make food, \q [though the] flock is cut off from [the] fold \q and there are no cattle in the stalls,
en.B: Though the fig tree does not flower and the vines bear no grapes, \q though the olive harvest fails \q and the fields yield nothing to eat, \q though the sheep vanish from the pen \q and the stalls hold no cattle,
en.R: The fig trees may not bloom, and there may be no grapes on the vines. \q The olive trees may give no olives, \q and the fields may produce no food. \q There may be no sheep in the pens \q and no cattle in the barns.

pt.L: Embora [a] figueira não dê flor e não haja colheita nas videiras, \q [embora] a produção da oliveira falhe \q e os campos não deem alimento, \q [embora] o rebanho seja arrancado do curral \q e não haja gado nas estrebarias,
pt.B: Embora a figueira não floresça e as videiras não deem uvas, \q embora a colheita das azeitonas fracasse \q e os campos não produzam nada para comer, \q embora as ovelhas desapareçam do curral \q e os estábulos fiquem sem gado,
pt.R: Pode ser que as figueiras não floresçam e que não haja uvas nas parreiras. \q Pode ser que as oliveiras não deem azeitonas \q e que os campos não produzam comida. \q Pode ser que não haja ovelhas nos currais \q nem gado nos estábulos.

decisions.choice: though: even if everything fails
decisions.reason: The verse lists everything a farming people lived on: figs, grapes, olives, grain, sheep and cattle (Deuteronomy 8:8; Joel 1:10-12). The word at the start may mean "though" or "for": either the prophet imagines the worst, or he describes the ruin the invasion will bring. Either way, verse 18 says that his joy does not depend on them.

decisions.choice: the flock is cut off from the fold
decisions.reason: The sheep and goats are gone from their pen, taken by the enemy or dead from want of pasture.

decisions.choice: Though (L, B); may (R); the comma at the end (L, B)
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 18, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma. Readable makes each line a sentence with "may" and begins verse 18 with "Even then".

decisions.choice: Embora (L, B); Pode ser que (R); the comma at the end (L, B)
decisions.reason: The verse is one of the best known in the book, so it was drafted from the Hebrew and the gloss and worded apart from the familiar Portuguese versions. "Embora" carries the concession of the opening word (m1) through each line; Literal brackets the repeated "embora", which the Hebrew does not repeat. As in the English, Literal and Balanced end with a comma and run on into verse 18, and Readable makes each line a sentence with "Pode ser que".

source.text: וַאֲנִ֖י בַּיהוָ֣ה אֶעְל֑וֹזָה אָגִ֖ילָה בֵּאלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׁעִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: yet I, in Yahweh I will exult; I will rejoice in [the] God of my salvation.

en.L: yet I, in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I will exult; \q I will rejoice in [the] God of my salvation.
en.B: yet I will rejoice in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q I will find joy in God, my Savior.
en.R: Even then I will be glad because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I will be joyful because God saves me.

pt.L: eu, porém, {{divine_name:no SENHOR|em Javé}} exultarei; \q encontrarei alegria no Deus da minha salvação.
pt.B: eu, mesmo assim, me alegrarei {{divine_name:no SENHOR|em Javé}}; \q encontrarei a minha alegria em Deus, o meu Salvador.
pt.R: Mesmo então, vou ficar contente por causa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. \q Vou ter alegria, porque Deus me salva.

decisions.choice: yet I will exult in the LORD: joy in God himself
decisions.reason: The prophet who began with complaint ends with joy. His joy rests not on the harvest or on his circumstances but on the LORD himself, the God who saves him (Psalm 73:25-26). "I" is emphatic in the Hebrew: whatever happens, I will rejoice.

decisions.choice: the God of my salvation: God who rescues me
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in verses 8 and 13 for the LORD's rescue of his people. The phrase is common in the Psalms (Psalm 18:47; 25:5).

decisions.choice: God, my Savior (B); because God saves me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "Savior" and "saves" for "salvation", the noun's sense here (m2).

source.text: יְהוִ֤הּאֲדֹנָי֙ חֵילִ֔י וַיָּ֤שֶׂם רַגְלַי֙ כָּֽאַיָּל֔וֹת וְעַ֥ל בָּמוֹתַ֖י יַדְרִכֵ֑נִי לַמְנַצֵּ֖חַ בִּנְגִינוֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh, [the] Lord, [is] my strength, and he makes my feet like the does, and on my high places he makes me tread. To the director, with my stringed instruments.

en.L: {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} my Lord [is] my strength, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes my feet like the does', \q and on my heights {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes me tread. \q For the director: with stringed instruments.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} is my strength; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes my feet as sure as a deer's \q and lets me walk on the heights. \q For the music director. With stringed instruments.
en.R: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} is my strength. \q He makes me sure-footed like a deer. \q He lets me walk safely high up in the mountains. \q For the leader of the music. To be played on stringed instruments.

pt.L: {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, meu Senhor, [é] a minha força, \q e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} torna os meus pés como os das corças, \q e sobre as minhas alturas {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me faz andar. \q Para o regente: com os meus instrumentos de cordas.
pt.B: O Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} é a minha força; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} torna os meus pés firmes como os da corça \q e me faz andar nas alturas. \q Para o mestre de música. Com instrumentos de cordas.
pt.R: O Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} é a minha força. \q Ele me dá pés firmes como os de uma corça. \q Ele me deixa andar em segurança no alto das montanhas. \q Para quem dirige a música. Para ser tocado com instrumentos de cordas.

decisions.choice: GOD my Lord: the divine name and the title
decisions.reason: Here the name comes before the title (*'Adonai*), as in Psalm 140:8. The name is then read aloud as "God" so as not to say "Lord" twice.

decisions.choice: my feet like the does', on my heights: the words of Psalm 18:34
decisions.reason: David says the same of God in Psalm 18:34 (2 Samuel 22:34): "making my feet like the does', and on my heights he makes me stand". Habakkuk says "tread" or "walk". The doe is sure-footed on steep, rocky heights; God gives him safety and strength to stand where others would fall. Deuteronomy 32:13 and Isaiah 58:14 speak of riding on the heights of the land.

decisions.choice: For the director: with stringed instruments: a note for the leader of the temple music
decisions.reason: The psalm closes with the kind of note that stands at the head of many psalms (Psalm 4:1): it is for the leader of the music, to be played on stringed instruments. Here it comes at the end, and the Hebrew says "my stringed instruments". It shows that the prayer was used in worship.

decisions.choice: GOD my Lord (L); the Lord GOD (B, R); the Psalm 18:34 wording
decisions.reason: As in Psalm 140:8, the name is written GOD so that the two are not read as "Lord Lord"; Balanced and Readable use the familiar order. The lines about the feet and the heights take the published wording of Psalm 18:34 at each level, with "tread" or "walk" for Habakkuk's verb.

decisions.choice: the Psalm 4:1 wording for the note
decisions.reason: The note to the director follows Psalm 4:1 at each level: "For the director: with stringed instruments" (Literal), "For the music director. With stringed instruments" (Balanced), "For the leader of the music. To be played on stringed instruments" (Readable). It stands as the last line of the verse.

decisions.choice: DEUS, meu Senhor (L); o Senhor DEUS (B, R); torna os meus pés como os das corças ... sobre as minhas alturas ... me faz (L); pés firmes como os da corça (B, R)
decisions.reason: The name and title follow Psalm 140:8 in Portuguese, "DEUS, meu Senhor" at Literal and "o Senhor DEUS" at Balanced and Readable (m1). The lines on the feet and the heights keep the Portuguese of Psalm 18:34 (m2), with "andar" for Habakkuk's "tread" and "corça" at every level for the doe of the Hebrew, where Psalm 18:34 has "cervo" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: Para o regente: com os meus instrumentos de cordas (L); Para o mestre de música. Com instrumentos de cordas (B); Para quem dirige a música. Para ser tocado com instrumentos de cordas (R)
decisions.reason: The closing note takes the wording of the Psalms' titles in Portuguese (Psalm 4:1) at each level (m3). Literal keeps the Hebrew "meus", which the English Literal leaves out.
